title: Analytics Events: What They Are and Why They Matter
description: What an analytics event is, how it differs from a pageview, and why GA4 and PostHog treat named actions as the unit of product insight.
quickAnswer: An **analytics event** is a named action you choose to record — signup, purchase, button click, or pageview. Pageviews are one kind of event; product analytics tools treat almost everything as events so you can build funnels, retention, and revenue reports.

sections.title: A simple definition
sections.content:
An **event** is a discrete thing that happened that you want to measure. Clicking "Start trial," completing checkout, watching a video, or loading a page can all be events.

Vendors disagree about defaults — some auto-capture many clicks, others only count pageviews unless you define goals — but the idea is the same: **name the action, attach useful context, analyze the counts**.

sections.title: Pageviews are events too
sections.content:
Classic web analytics centers on **pageviews** and sessions. Modern tools (including GA4) model a pageview as an event with properties like URL, title, and referrer.

That shift matters because the same pipeline can then track:

- Marketing goals (newsletter signup)
- Product actions (created project, invited teammate)
- Revenue (purchase completed)

If you only need "how many people visited /blog," a pageview-first tool like Plausible is enough. If you need "how many invited a teammate within 7 days of signup," you need custom events — and usually a product analytics tool.

sections.title: Anatomy of a useful event
sections.content:
A durable event usually has:

1. **A stable name** — e.g. `signup_completed`, not `click_button_3`
2. **Properties** — plan tier, source, error code, value
3. **Identity rules** — anonymous visitor vs logged-in user
4. **A reason to exist** — a decision or dashboard that depends on it

Naming discipline beats volume. Ten well-named events outperform a hundred noisy autocaptured clicks you never trust.

sections.title: Where tools differ
sections.content:
**GA4** is event-based by design and free at high volume, with deep Google Ads ties. Setup and reporting take learning.

**PostHog** is built for product events, funnels, replay, and flags — stronger inside SaaS apps, heavier script and instrumentation tax.

**Plausible / Fathom** emphasize pageviews and simple goals; custom events exist but the product stays marketing-site focused.

**DataFast** tracks traffic and optional payment-linked revenue events for indie SaaS — different primary question than product funnels.

Read the head-to-heads when you are choosing a stack; this primer is only the vocabulary.

sections.title: What to do next
sections.content:
1. List the 5–10 actions that change a business decision (not every click).
2. Decide whether you need **web** analytics, **product** analytics, or both.
3. Compare tools that match that job — then check [pricing](/calculators/pricing/) and [recorded script benchmarks](/benchmarks/).

For the vocabulary gap between counting pages and counting actions, see [Pageviews vs Events: Which Should You Track?](/learn/pageviews-vs-events/).
